title: Tesla Trade Options Review 2026: Is It Safe to Sign Up?
description: Tesla Trade Options review: what its site claims about a $250 deposit, AI trading and a 4.6/5 rating, and what to check before you sign up.
author: James Whitmore
excerpt: Tesla Trade Options promotes AI trading with a $250 minimum and a 4.6/5 rating, but names no operator or regulator.
content:
Tesla Trade Options is presented as an AI-assisted trading platform with automated trades, a demo account and a $250 starting point. The page names no operator, regulator or licence, and offers just a 4.6/5 rating as its performance figure, with no source.

The name refers to Tesla options, but the page does not mention Tesla or describe any option contract. It describes a general crypto and multi-asset tool. The following sets out the page's claims and flags those we could not establish.

Tesla Trade Options at a Glance

Here is what the platform's own page states and what it leaves out.

CategoryWhat the page says
Platform typeAI-assisted trading with automatic and manual modes
Minimum deposit$250, currency not named
FeesNone stated. No schedule given
Payment methodsCards, PayPal, Skrill and bank transfer, with other options unnamed
WithdrawalsUsually within 24 hours. No limits given
SupportDescribed as 24/7, with no channels listed
Regulator or licenceNot stated
OperatorNot named

Items come from the platform's own page. We have not tested the platform.

Is Tesla Trade Options Legit? What the Claims Show

Automation and signals

The page says AI and machine learning generate signals and can place trades automatically, with a manual mode for users who prefer control. The page omits its strategy, model and risk limits, so the claim stands untested.

Performance and ratings

The page refers to a high success rate and notable gains from a small deposit, but gives no return figures, time period, sample size or method. Neither a source nor a review count accompanies the 4.6/5 figure.

Asset coverage

The name refers to Tesla options, but the page does not mention Tesla or describe any option contract. It describes a general crypto and multi-asset tool. The list of markets you can actually trade is not shown before you register.

Costs and Minimum Deposit

The page states a $250 minimum deposit and says there are no registration, transaction or withdrawal fees. The page leaves out spreads, a fee schedule and any payment-provider charges.

We treat 250 as the usual minimum in each market, so readers see AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU. The $250 figure comes without a currency, and the terms should be read for the exact amount first.

Who Is Behind Tesla Trade Options

The page names no legal entity, company number or address. Registration links go to coinpulse.cc, a third-party domain, and nothing reveals whether the publisher benefits from them.

Is Tesla Trade Options a Scam? Withdrawals and Complaints

Searches for Tesla Trade Options often ask whether it is a scam, whether withdrawals work and whether there are complaints. A day is the typical withdrawal time the page gives, while limits, timelines and complaints are not covered.

Prior to any deposit, examine complaint records and reviews that identify their sources. Positive testimonials and scores do not tell you how withdrawal requests are managed.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal company behind Tesla Trade Options and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • Insist on a written fee schedule, spreads included, before you commit.
  • Request performance records that you can test and that show their dates.
  • Keep the opening stake minimal and practise on the demo before using real money.

Risks to Keep in Mind

The main risk is an unnamed operator, because a user has no clear party to hold to account. That risk is heightened by the mismatches within the page's claims. Automated trades can still lose money just as manual ones can.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Tesla Trade Options legit?

The site makes claims about Tesla Trade Options but names no operator, regulator or licence number. The company registry and the regulator's register should both be checked before you fund anything.

What is the minimum deposit for Tesla Trade Options?

The page does not specify a currency for the $250 amount. Confirm both the figure and the currency from the terms before you pay anything.

Is Tesla Trade Options regulated?

A regulator and licence are missing from the page, which also refers to brokers without naming them. Use your national regulator's register to confirm who runs the service.

Does Tesla Trade Options charge fees?

A claim of no fees sits beside the absence of any schedule for spreads, withdrawals or conversion. Read the full terms first.

Does automating trades cancel the risk of losing money?

No. Automated trades can still lose money just as manual ones can.

Our Verdict on Tesla Trade Options

Tesla Trade Options's page makes broad claims without naming an operator, a regulator or verifiable results. Our rating reflects these gaps. Once the operator and its claims can be confirmed, we will update this page. Limit yourself to money you can comfortably afford to lose.
